IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Possible tenant data overlap reported by customer CoreHealth (cust-4912). Hits show mixed 200 responses containing other-customer session fragments. Severity: P1. Please respond in-thread. thread_ts=1769990000

Ben (on-call SRE): I'm on it. Acknowledging pager. Setting bridge and paging runtime + security. 

Carmen (runtime eng): Saw the alert from infra metrics. Quick ask — is this observed on Hosted API only or Dedicated pools too?

Ben (on-call SRE): Initial signal from support indicates CoreHealth hit Hosted API endpoint behind shared edge gateway. No Dedicated pool mention yet. Putting client-facing traffic on hold for this customer if needed. :eyes:

Luis (Support): CoreHealth reported seeing another tenant's prompt in response body. They pasted a snippet but redacted some parts. Ticket created: SR-8421. I'm on standby to coordinate customer comms.

Deepa (Security): Need logs and raw responses. If there's evidence of cross-tenant leakage we escalate immediately. Carmen, can you pull gateway logs for the last 10 minutes and grep for cust-4912?

Carmen (runtime eng): Pulling now. Partial logs below:
```
2026-06-15T14:05:12Z req_id=abc123 tenant_hint=cust-4912 route=shared-gw session_prefix=svc/tenant/789 payload_len=204
2026-06-15T14:05:12Z req_id=abc123 backend_call=pool-shared:7 target_tenant=svc/tenant/123 kv_read=svc/tenant/123/config -> 200
2026-06-15T14:05:12Z req_id=abc123 response_snippet="...<PROMPT FROM OTHER CUST REDACTED>..."
```
Looks like a backend call returned a cached object from a different tenant prefix. Not typical.

Priya (Dedicated Ops): If shared-gw is resolving session_prefix incorrectly we might be falling back to a legacy routing table. I can temporarily drain shared pool nodes to isolate traffic. Recommend: 1) Drain pool-shared:7 2) Enable strict header-based tenant enforcement on edge for session_prefix -> tenant mapping 3) Live-rotate cache entries.

Marco (Networking): I'm checking the edge LB rules. There's a recent change from this morning that added a longest-prefix rewrite for `/svc/tenant/` patterns. Possible regression: rewrite might strip tenant id in the backend key. Pulling HAProxy logs now.

Carmen (runtime eng): Gate log shows HAProxy forwarded header `X-Tenant-Prefix: svc/tenant/789` but our cache key normalization code had a fallback that normalizes unknown prefixes to `svc/tenant/123` when pattern match fails. That fallback shouldn't be used in production. Suspect a bad regex introduced in deploy 2026-06-15T12:00.

Deepa (Security): Evidence looks like routing + cache normalization bug. Potential exposure surface: any cached model prompt or output stored under normalized key could surface. We need immediate mitigation. Recommend temporary stop of writes to shared cache and eviction of keys that match `svc/tenant/*`.

Ben (on-call SRE): Executing mitigations: 1) Offlining pool-shared:7 2) Turning cache writes to read-only 3) Applying ephemeral firewall rule to drop traffic matching rewrite rule. Running commands now: 
```
./ctl pool drain --pool pool-shared:7 --reason "isolation - cust-4912 suspected overlap" --now
./cachectl mode set --scope shared --mode read-only
sudo iptables -A INPUT -m string --string "rewrite:strip-tenant" --algo bm -j DROP
```
Command results: drain started (nodes 3/3 draining), cache mode set, firewall rule applied.

Priya (Dedicated Ops): Confirmed drain progressing. New requests are being routed to alternate pools with header enforcement.

Ben (on-call SRE): Quick smoke test against CoreHealth request path (simulated):
```
curl -s -H "X-Tenant-ID: cust-4912" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.test/v1/infer -d '{"prompt":"whoami"}'
```
Response now returns only tenant-local content. No cross-tenant fragments.

Jake (CSM): I've messaged CoreHealth: "We've taken your traffic off the shared node and applied an isolation mitigation. Your service will remain available via alternate nodes; we're running a remediation and will follow up with RCA."

Luis (Support): CoreHealth acknowledged the mitigation and asked for ETA on full restore. I told them we'll aim for under 2 hours for remediation and will update every 30 minutes.

Deepa (Security): Create an evidence bundle. Carmen, export the related logs and capture the exact cached key values. We'll need hashes for forensics. Also create a timeline.

Carmen (runtime eng): Export in progress. Example offending key observed: `cache://svc/tenant/123/prompt:xyz` which was returned on request for `svc/tenant/789`. I'm zipping logs now and uploading to internal secure bucket `s3://redwood-incident-evidence/1769990000/`.

Marco (Networking): Reverted this morning's LB rewrite as a precaution. Planning a quick fix to normalization code to remove the unsafe fallback.

Priya (Dedicated Ops): Once drain completes, I'll rotate caches and re-enable writes behind tightened header checks. Post-checklist: 1) confirm no cross-tenant read traces in logs 2) run synthetic queries against 50 random tenants 3) bring pool back to service with canary.

Deepa (Security): Opening INC-2026-3427 and linking evidence. We'll run full scope assessment to determine if any PII left the tenant boundary. If confirmed exposure -> notify legal and follow customer breach protocol.

Ben (on-call SRE): Summary / next steps in thread: - Mitigation applied (drain + cache read-only + firewall + LB revert) - Evidence collected and uploaded - Customer notified and on-call handling comms - Postmortem scheduled at 1600 UTC today. Assigning owners: Carmen -> runtime fix + logs, Marco -> LB rule revert + config patch, Priya -> pool restore + cache rotation, Deepa -> forensics + compliance, Jake/Luis -> customer comms.

Jake (CSM): I'll coordinate with CoreHealth for postmortem review and share timeline.

Carmen (runtime eng): Quick note: found the bad regex in commit `a1b2c3f` (deploy 2026-06-15T11:58). I'll prepare a rollback/patch PR and request an expedited review.

Ben (on-call SRE): Good. Keep updates in-thread. If anyone needs additional hands request now. Otherwise we'll close the bridge once pools restored and synthetic checks pass. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident record created: INC-2026-3427. Pager cleared by Ben at 1769990125.
